message.content: {"parent_id":"r0_b0","target_witnesses":["r1_witness_1","r1_witness_0","r1_witness_2"],"concept":"Output-history adaptation","explanation":"The approximate collisions show different estimated drifts at similar x and u=0, but do not identify what history matters. A competing account is that the system retains a filtered trace of its own past output rather than a filtered trace of past input. Here z0 tracks x and contributes to dx/dt. This can make drift depend on how the system reached its current x, while differing structurally from the parent’s input-driven memory. The observations do not establish this mechanism, and the close but unequal x values and noisy derivative estimates limit the witness evidence.","analogy":{"domain":"adaptive control","relation":"an internal state tracks recent output and modifies subsequent response","mapping":"z0 is an exponentially filtered trace of x, with rate x-p0*z0; its contribution to dx/dt represents output-history-dependent adaptation","breaks_when":"response depends on input history independently of the output trajectory, or on history features that a single exponential trace cannot represent"},"provenance":"model_knowledge_unverified","spec":{"parameters":[{"name":"p0","lower":0.05,"initial":0.8,"upper":3.0}],"states":[{"name":"z0","meaning":"Exponentially filtered history of the observed state x, initialized to zero; unlike the parent state, it is not directly driven by u.","rate":"x-p0*z0"}],"terms":["1","x","u","z0"]},"distinguishing_prediction":"Compare trials with different input schedules that produce closely matched x and u=0 but different filtered x histories. This model predicts drift differences associated with those x histories; the parent input-trace model instead predicts differences according to residual filtered input. In particular, schedules producing similar x histories but different input traces should tend to have similar drift under this model, but not necessarily under the parent.","falsifier":"Across repeated, sufficiently resolved trials, drift differences at matched x and u consistently track residual input history even when filtered x histories are similar, while differing filtered x histories do not predict drift variation.","limitations":"This is a competing, unverified one-state account, not evidence that output-history adaptation exists. Filtered x and filtered input may be strongly correlated in the supplied trajectories, and approximate state matches and smoothed noisy derivatives make the witnesses inconclusive. Complete held-out trajectory performance would be needed to compare the accounts."}
